paper_source.basis: Supplementary Figure 1 and Note 2: 80/20 frame, acrylic base, outboard hollow uprights movable relative to emitter, custom 1.5 mm Al reflector track. Figure labels a 305 mm inner span. Text says approximately 150 mm reflector height while the figure labels 100 mm; historical geometry is ambiguous.

9 x 9 x 3 mm, M5 x 0.8. Open rail ends must remain accessible for initial insertion.

9.32 mm head diameter, 2.63 mm height, 3 mm hex, M5 x 0.8. Linked product is 10 mm; this reconstruction selects 8, 16 and 40 mm lengths, with a smooth nominal full-thread envelope and inferred dome/drive depth.

author_choices: Do not trace an undimensioned product illustration: use nominal rail dimensions. Outer radius 1.5 mm and four bore lobes at +/-1.65 mm with radius 0.85 mm are inferred. Slot end blends and 2-degree drop-lock compliance are not reconstructed; calculated area/inertia are diagnostics only.

A sharp 9 x 9 x 3 mm T-nut envelope intersects the nominal diagonal web; the failed mesh is retained. A 0.25 mm deep-side chamfer is selected to clear it, but is not a confirmed manufacturer feature. Real product chamfer and tolerance compatibility still need source CAD or metrology before fit acceptance.

Keep 305 x 280 x 6 mm base and central-jack mounting. Move rails to the base-bottom plane: rails Z24..44 mm, base Z24..30 mm, nominal inner span 305 mm. Exact edge contact has no manufacturing tolerance allowance yet.

Four original 42 x 20 x 3 mm bridge plates below the base, with 22 mm hole spacing, attach the base to real lower rail slots. These replace an inapplicable offset panel-retainer selection; no 20-2496 model is claimed.

Original ordinary machined split clamps attach the rods to outer rail slots. Lower blocks are 35 x 50 x 20 mm; upper caps 35 x 30 x 20 mm with a 17 mm blind bore and 3 mm shoulder. They are apparatus parts, not robot-specific fixtures or a commercial product identity.

Selected 20/14 mm hollow tubes have a 0.2 mm diametral open-clamp allowance. Clamp deformation and tightening are not solved. Tube ends support the upper-cap shoulders; selected cut length follows the retained reflector height.

Extend the inferred track path to 395 mm between outboard uprights and add true mounting holes. Track curvature and fixed band path are still a site/date design hypothesis; historical path is not known.

Replace the unretained legacy reflector carriage with two original 20 x 20 mm clamp plates, tapped lower holes and two M3 x 10 countersunk screws. Countersinks continue through the 1 mm reflector into its backing plate. Two screw heads remain visible and flush; their optical effect is not assessed. Repositioning needs screw loosening; friction, travel and tool access are unqualified.
Four ordinary SJ5017 feet on acrylic avoid supporting the apparatus on screw heads; adhesion, compression, horizontal stability and weather exposure remain unqualified.
